Midweek, working rules for crate labels
This section shows the main rule first, then the reasons
Companion Animal Travel Desk: crate checks and humane handling

This section sets the required desk practice for animal travel records, crate labels, and handoff notes so that every moving case is handled in a calm, orderly, and humane manner. The main rule is that each crate must be checked against the booking record before acceptance, and every label must be clear, legible, and matched to the correct traveler and animal. If a label is worn, loose, or incomplete, staff must stop the transfer, secure the item, and correct the record before the animal moves onward.

Handlers must use calm methods at all times, keep voices low, and avoid sudden motion around the animal or the crate. The desk must never rush a live animal past a welfare concern, and no staff member may override a comfort warning from the welfare coordinator. That review is required whenever species, temperament, or visible stress suggests that a care plan needs adjustment. Staff must record any feeding note, bedding note, or space note that affects welfare, and they must pass the note forward without delay.

Travelers may be asked to confirm their own contact details, but the desk shall rely on the approved record rather than informal statements when a discrepancy appears. If a traveler such as Hana Ramos or Zain Wilson reports a problem, the record aide must note the report at once and notify the senior coordinator. If a pet such as Moose arrives distressed, staff must prioritize quiet separation, water access when permitted, and a prompt welfare review. No crate may be treated as ordinary baggage when an animal is inside it.

The records aide must keep all entries complete, factual, and readable. Corrections are to be made by line-through and initials, never by erasure or guesswork. The Companion Animal Travel Desk must protect chain of custody, preserve humane handling, and ensure that every handoff leaves a trace in the file. Contact the welfare coordinator or the senior coordinator immediately for any exception, mismatch, or urgent animal concern.
